Qualitative research measures quantities; quantitative explores meanings.
Quantitative research uses words; qualitative uses numbers.
questions.answer: Qualitative research is exploratory and context-rich; quantitative focuses on measurement and statistical testing.

questions.question: Which sequence shows the most correct order of early steps in a typical research process?
options: Write research report → Conduct literature review → Collect data → Submit
Identify a research topic → Conduct a preliminary literature review → Formulate research question/hypothesis → Select methodology → Design plan
Collect data → Formulate research question → Analyze data → Write report
Present → Collect data → Interpret results → Design research plan
questions.answer: Identify a research topic → Conduct a preliminary literature review → Formulate research question/hypothesis → Select methodology → Design plan

questions.question: Which statement best describes reliability vs validity?
options: Reliability and validity mean the same thing
Reliability = producing consistent results across repeated measures; Validity = actually measuring the concept you want to measure
Reliability = measuring what you intend to measure; Validity = producing consistent results
Reliability refers to statistical significance; validity refers to practical significance
questions.answer: Reliability = producing consistent results across repeated measures; Validity = actually measuring the concept you want to measure

questions.question: Which of the following is a measure of dispersion?
options: Proportion
Standard deviation
Mode
Mean
questions.answer: Standard deviation

questions.question: Which of the following best defines research?
options: Copying existing reports and combining them into one document
A systematic process of investigating and analyzing information to answer questions, solve problems, or generate new knowledge
A random collection of facts for a school project
Giving presentations about what other people discovered
questions.answer: A systematic process of investigating and analyzing information to answer questions, solve problems, or generate new knowledge

questions.question: A researcher wants to compare the average number of competitions entered by students who actively use social media for skill-building versus those who do not. Which statistical test is most appropriate (assuming normality and equal variances)?
options: One-way ANOVA with three unrelated groups
Independent-samples t-test
Chi-square test
Pearson correlation coefficient
questions.answer: Independent-samples t-test

questions.question: Which component of a proposal explains why the chosen methods are appropriate and how data will be analyzed?
options: Acknowledgments
Methodology section
Title page
References
questions.answer: Methodology section

questions.question: An observational study finds a positive correlation between time spent watching YouTube tutorials and coding skill scores. Which statement is correct?
options: The correlation proves that tutorials are always accurate.
Correlation does not imply causation; further experimental or longitudinal study is needed to infer causality.
You can conclude YouTube watching causes improved coding skills.
You can conclude coding skills cause people to watch YouTube.
questions.answer: Correlation does not imply causation; further experimental or longitudinal study is needed to infer causality.

questions.question: A researcher studies lettuce yield under two LED spectra: full-spectrum white and red-blue mix. Which of the following correctly identifies the independent and dependent variables?
options: IV = growth medium; DV = LED spectrum.
IV = LED spectrum; DV = lettuce yield.
IV = lettuce yield; DV = LED spectrum.
IV = sample size; DV = LED spectrum.
questions.answer: IV = LED spectrum; DV = lettuce yield.

questions.question: If a study reports a p-value of 0.03 for the effect of social media on participation, which is the correct interpretation?
options: The alternative hypothesis is definitely true.
There is a 3% probability of obtaining the observed data (or more extreme) if the null hypothesis is true.
There is a 3% chance the null hypothesis is true.
The results are practically important.
questions.answer: There is a 3% probability of obtaining the observed data (or more extreme) if the null hypothesis is true.

questions.question: Which section of a research proposal should briefly summarize key aims, methods, and expected outcomes?
options: References
Abstract
Title
Literature review
questions.answer: Abstract

questions.question: A survey uses a Likert scale (Strongly disagree → Strongly agree). What level of measurement is this typically considered?
options: Interval with equal units guaranteed
Ordinal
Nominal
Ratio with a true zero
questions.answer: Ordinal

questions.question: Which of the following is not a primary purpose of a literature review?
options: Contextualizing the research problem
Replicating the exact text of prior studies verbatim
Identifying gaps in existing research
Understanding methodologies used by others
questions.answer: Replicating the exact text of prior studies verbatim

questions.question: In the Jemmy social-media scenario: “How are high school students using social media and does it influence their participation in international activities?” — identify the most likely independent and dependent variables.
options: Independent: Students’ school subject; Dependent: Country of residence
Independent: Use of social media platforms (YouTube, Discord, etc.); Dependent: Development of skills / participation in international competitions
Independent: Participation in international activities; Dependent: Use of social media
Independent: Time of day; Dependent: Platform logo color
questions.answer: Independent: Use of social media platforms (YouTube, Discord, etc.); Dependent: Development of skills / participation in international competitions

questions.question: Which test is most appropriate to check normality for a dataset of 30 observations?
options: Chi-square test
Shapiro–Wilk test
Kolmogorov–Smirnov test
Wilcoxon signed-rank test
questions.answer: Shapiro–Wilk test

questions.question: Which of these is most essential from an ethics perspective when conducting interviews with high school students about online competition participation?
options: Requiring participation as part of class grade without alternative
Obtaining informed consent (and parental consent if minors), ensuring privacy, and explaining voluntary participation and risks/benefits
Using complex legal documents to frighten them into participation
Publishing full names and transcripts without permission because it’s “for research”
questions.answer: Obtaining informed consent (and parental consent if minors), ensuring privacy, and explaining voluntary participation and risks/benefits

questions.question: Which of the following is a primary data source?
options: A meta-analysis published in a journal
Observations you collect in person for your study
National census dataset downloaded from government website
A literature review chapter from a thesis
questions.answer: Observations you collect in person for your study

questions.question: Which method is most appropriate if a researcher wants to measure how many hours students spend on social media per week and relate that to a standardized skill score?
options: Archival literary analysis only
Quantitative (surveys and standardized tests)
Qualitative (in-depth interviews only)
Purely observational field notes with no numbers
questions.answer: Quantitative (surveys and standardized tests)

questions.question: Why is a research proposal written before conducting the full study?
options: To replace the final report
To provide a clear plan of goals, methods, timeline and resources
To guarantee the research will be published
To avoid doing a literature review
questions.answer: To provide a clear plan of goals, methods, timeline and resources

questions.question: A sample of 25 students has a sample mean score of 70 and a sample standard deviation of 10. Using a t-critical value of 2.064 for 95% confidence (df = 24), what is the 95% confidence interval for the population mean?
Which section of the proposal most often includes a Gantt chart or schedule for tasks and milestones?
options: Methodology
Timeline (or Project Timeline)
Introduction
References
questions.answer: Timeline (or Project Timeline)

questions.question: For two independent groups with non-normal distributions, which test is most suitable to compare central tendency?
options: ANOVA
Mann–Whitney U test
Independent samples t-test
Paired samples t-test
questions.answer: Mann–Whitney U test

questions.question: Which statement about parametric vs nonparametric tests is correct?
options: Nonparametric tests assume data are normally distributed.
Parametric tests generally have more statistical power if assumptions hold.
Parametric tests never require normality.
Nonparametric tests always provide effect size measures directly.
questions.answer: Parametric tests generally have more statistical power if assumptions hold.

questions.question: Given sample test scores: 62, 70, 68, 75, 65. What is the mean score?
A researcher plans to compare mean test scores between two independent groups. Which statistical test is usually appropriate (assuming normality and equal variances)?
options: One-way ANOVA for three groups only
Independent samples t-test
Chi-square test
Pearson correlation
questions.answer: Independent samples t-test

questions.question: Which statistical test is most appropriate to compare mean lettuce yields between two independent groups (full-spectrum vs red-blue), when sample sizes are small and data are approximately normally distributed?
options: Chi-square test
Independent (two-sample) t-test
Paired t-test
Pearson correlation
questions.answer: Independent (two-sample) t-test

questions.question: Interpretation of a p-value of 0.03 (with α = 0.05):
options: The effect is practically important.
There is strong evidence against the null, so reject the null at α = 0.05.
The null hypothesis is definitely true.
There is a 3% probability the alternative hypothesis is true.
questions.answer: There is strong evidence against the null, so reject the null at α = 0.05.
